title: Constructible domains for the two-stage algebraic-closure proper comparison
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$, a field $k$ of characteristic $p>0$ with $p\ne\ell$, and an algebraic closure $\Omega/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with its extended $\ell$-adic norm topology. Schemes are separated and finite type over $k$ and morphisms are $k$-morphisms [sk-def-sfb-dc-setting]. For a profinite set $S$ put
$$C(S)=\{a\in C(S,\Omega):a(S)\subset F\text{ for some finite intermediate field }\mathbf Q_\ell\subset F\subset\Omega\},\qquad B(S)=C(S,\Omega).$$
Here $C$ is the finite-subextension-valued condensed ring [sk-def-sfb-qlbar-condensed], $B$ uses ALL norm-continuous maps [def-sfb-continuous-map-condensed-ring], and $c:C\to B$ is inclusion. Put $R_W=p_W^*R$ for every coefficient ring $R$ [sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients]. Use ordinary unbounded derived categories of internal module objects and their derived geometric adjunctions [sk-def-sfb-module-objects, sk-def-sfb-module-derived-pushpull]. Let $D^b_c(W,R)$ be the full subcategory of complexes with bounded constructible cohomology, where constructible means finite constant local models on finite constructible locally closed stratifications [sk-def-sfb-constructible], and finite Tor amplitude is the vanishing of $H^q(K\otimes^{\mathbf L}_{R_W}N)$ outside a bounded interval for all $R_W$-modules $N$ [det-def-sfb-constructible-tor-amplitude]. Write $J_W=B_W\otimes^L_{C_W}-$ for the actual K-flat derived extension [sk-def-sfb-derived-extension-of-scalars].

Fix a finite intermediate field $E\subset\Omega$ with the restricted norm topology, put $A_E(S)=C(S,E)$, and let $a:A_E\to C$ be inclusion of functions. Write $S_W=C_W\otimes^L_{A_{E,W}}-$. For a proper morphism $f:Z\to T$ [def-weil-proper-morphism] and $K\in D^b_c(Z,A_E)$ put
$$L=S_ZK,\qquad P=Rf_{*,C}L,\qquad Q=Rf_{*,B}J_ZL.$$
Let $\chi_{a,K}:S_TRf_{*,A_E}K\to P$ be the canonical counit mate: its adjunct under $f_C^*\dashv Rf_{*,C}$ is the canonical pullback/tensor comparison $f_C^*S_TRf_{*,A_E}K\cong S_Zf_{A_E}^*Rf_{*,A_E}K$ followed by $S_Z\varepsilon_{A_E,K}$, with the K-flat balanced-tensor normalization [lem-pur-ringed-coefficient-projection-cocycle]. Then $L\in D^b_c(Z,C)$, $P\in D^b_c(T,C)$, and $\chi_{a,K}$ is an isomorphism. Moreover $J_ZL\in D^b_c(Z,B)$ has finite Tor amplitude, and both $J_TP$ and $Q$ belong to $D^b_c(T,B)$. These are assertions in the ordinary ambient derived categories; no flatness of either coefficient inclusion is assumed.

proof.text: The field $k$ is Noetherian: an ideal containing a nonzero element contains $1$, so its only ideals are $0$ and $k$. Thus $\operatorname{Spec}k$ is locally Noetherian by [pqf-def-locnoeth], and it is quasi-compact by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-scheme-qcqs]. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian] to the finite-type structure maps of $Z,T$: both schemes are Noetherian. Also [pqf-lem-proper-basic] makes the given proper $f$ quasi-compact and quasi-separated.

proof.text: The rational-category identification in [sk-thm-sfb-qlbar-two-colimit] (4) identifies the finite-constant-model $D^b_c$ and $D^b_{ctf}$ categories for $A_E,C$ with the ordinary bounded constructible categories used in the finite-subextension results. The coefficient $C$ here is precisely that theorem's finite-subextension-valued algebraic closure, not $B$. By [def-sfb-derived-extend-to-qlbar], its functor $T_{E,\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell}$ is exactly $S_Z$. Apply [lem-sfb-extend-to-qlbar-constructible] to $K$ to obtain $L=S_ZK\in D^b_c(Z,C)$.

proof.text: Apply [det-thm-sfb-proper-base-change-rational] (2) with $\Lambda=C$ and the proper morphism $f$. It gives $P=Rf_{*,C}L$ bounded constructible. The identification of its constructibility convention with finite constant local models is [sk-thm-sfb-qlbar-two-colimit] (4), now on $T$.

source.place: Paragraph (3): intermediate proper-image finiteness; agent assembly from the cited DAG statements

proof.text: Since $K$ is bounded, it is bounded below. The qcqs comparison [lem-sfb-qlbar-direct-image-comparison], with the given $E\subset\Omega$, therefore gives an isomorphism $S_TRf_{*,A_E}K\to Rf_{*,C}S_ZK=P$. This is the required $\chi_{a,K}$: the cited statement specifies the adjunct of scalar extension of the $A_E$-counit under the canonical pullback/tensor identification. That is exactly the defining adjunct in the item, so uniqueness of adjuncts identifies the maps. No ambient unbounded coproduct-continuity hypothesis is invoked, and the coefficient on this step is $C$.

source.place: Paragraph (3): intermediate coefficient comparison, with the counit mate fixed; agent assembly from the cited DAG statements

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-constructible-algcl-topology-comparison] on $Z$ to $L$ and on $T$ to $P$. Its actual K-flat functors are the $J_Z,J_T$ of the item, so $J_ZL\in D^b_c(Z,B)$ and $J_TP\in D^b_c(T,B)$. Because $Z$ is Noetherian by step 1, [det-sf-comp-continuous-algcl-constructible-tor] applied to $J_ZL$ gives finite Tor amplitude. This uses the ring of ALL continuous norm-valued maps, with no claim that $C=B$ or that $c$ is flat.

source.place: Paragraph (3): domains of the topology-change functor and finite Tor amplitude; agent assembly from the cited DAG statements

proof.text: The input $J_ZL$ is bounded constant-model constructible with finite Tor amplitude by step 5. Apply the preservation clause of [det-sf-comp-proper-continuous-algcl] to the proper $k$-morphism $f$ and the all-continuous ring $B$. It gives $Q=Rf_{*,B}J_ZL\in D^b_c(T,B)$ (indeed with finite Tor amplitude). Together with steps 2--5 this proves every stated conclusion in the ordinary ambient derived categories.
